## Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(tmap)
library(tmaptools)
library(sf)

```

## Test objects 

```{r}
A <- 1
B <- 2
C <- A + B
C
ls()

```

## Plot and data frames

```{r}
Data1 <- c(1:100)
Data2 <- c(101:200)
plot(Data1, Data2, col = "red")

df <- data.frame(Data1, Data2)
df %>% head()
df[1:10, 1]
df %>% dplyr::rename(column1 = Data1, column2 = Data2) -> df
df %>% dplyr::select(column1)

```

## Download the data

Here I get the London Ward Profiles Excel file from the London Datastore (I choose the easy route by reading the csv straight from the web using the URL).

```{r}
LondonData <- read_csv("https://data.london.gov.uk/download/f33fb38c-cb37-48e3-8298-84c0d3cc5a6c/772d2d64-e8c6-46cb-86f9-e52b4c7851bc/ward-profiles-excel-version.csv",
                       locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
                       na = "n/a")

```

## Check it loaded properly

```{r}
class(LondonData)
Datatypelist <- LondonData %>%
  summarise_all(class) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "All_variables", values_to = "Variable_class")
Datatypelist

```

## Selecte the relevant boroughs

Here I start to manipulate with dplyr.

```{r}
library(stringr)
LondonBoroughs <- LondonData %>%
  filter(str_detect(`New code`, "^E09")) %>%
  distinct()
LondonBoroughs$`Ward name`

```

## Rename and tidy the column names

```{r}
LondonBoroughs <- LondonBoroughs %>%
  dplyr::rename(Borough = `Ward name`) %>%
  clean_names()
colnames(LondonBoroughs)

```

## Calculate life expectancy values

```{r}
Life_expectancy <- LondonBoroughs %>%
  mutate(averagelifeexpectancy = (female_life_expectancy_2009_13 + male_life_expectancy_2009_13) / 2) %>%
  mutate(normalisedlifeepectancy = averagelifeexpectancy / mean(averagelifeexpectancy)) %>%
  dplyr::select(new_code, borough, averagelifeexpectancy, normalisedlifeepectancy) %>%
  arrange(desc(normalisedlifeepectancy))

slice_head(Life_expectancy, n = 5)
slice_tail(Life_expectancy, n = 5)

```

## Compare to the UK average (81.16)

```{r}
Life_expectancy2 <- Life_expectancy %>%
  mutate(UKcompare = case_when(averagelifeexpectancy > 81.16 ~ "above UK average",
                               TRUE ~ "below UK average"))

Life_expectancy2_group <- Life_expectancy2 %>%
  mutate(UKdiff = averagelifeexpectancy - 81.16) %>%
  group_by(UKcompare) %>%
  summarise(range = max(UKdiff) - min(UKdiff), count = n(), Average = mean(UKdiff))
Life_expectancy2_group

```

## Build version for the map

```{r}
Life_expectancy4 <- Life_expectancy %>%
  mutate(UKdiff = averagelifeexpectancy - 81.16) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(across(UKdiff, \(x) round(x, 0)))

```

## Quick plot

```{r}
plot(LondonBoroughs$male_life_expectancy_2009_13,
     LondonBoroughs$percent_children_in_reception_year_who_are_obese_2011_12_to_2013_14)

```

## Read in boundary files

I got the Local Authority Districts (Dec 2015) full clipped boundaries for Great Britain from the ONS Open Geography Portal, as a shapefile. 

```{r}
EW <- st_read("prac2_data/LAD_Dec_2015_FCB_GB_2022_-5677438911922075002")

```

## Pull out London and plot

```{r}
LondonMap <- EW %>% filter(str_detect(lad15cd, "^E09"))
qtm(LondonMap)

```

## Join data to the boundaries

```{r}
LondonData <- clean_names(LondonData)

BoroughDataMap <- EW %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  filter(str_detect(lad15cd, "^E09")) %>%
  left_join(., LondonData, by = c("lad15cd" = "new_code")) %>%
  distinct(., lad15cd, .keep_all = TRUE)

nrow(BoroughDataMap)   # should be 33

```

## Quick map

```{r}
tmap_mode("plot")
qtm(BoroughDataMap, fill = "rate_of_job_seekers_allowance_jsa_claimants_2015")

```

## Interactive map

```{r}
BoroughDataMap84 <- BoroughDataMap %>% st_transform(., 4326)

tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(BoroughDataMap84) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "rate_of_job_seekers_allowance_jsa_claimants_2015",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.bu_pu", style = "jenks"),
              fill_alpha = 0.5,
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Job seekers' Allowance Claimants", size = 0.8)) +
  tm_basemap(server = "OpenStreetMap") +
  tm_title("Job seekers' Allowance Claimants")

```

## Map life expectancy data

```{r}
Life_expectancy4map <- EW %>%
  inner_join(., Life_expectancy4, by = c("lad15cd" = "new_code")) %>%
  distinct(., lad15cd, .keep_all = TRUE)

tmap_mode("plot")
tm_shape(Life_expectancy4map) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "UKdiff",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.bu_pu", style = "jenks"),
              fill_alpha = 0.5,
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Number of years")) +
  tm_title("Difference in life expectancy")

```

## Read flytipping data with set column types

This section uses the web version of the flytipping data, not my pivot-table export, because it has the columns code, area, year, total_incidents, and so on.

```{r}
flytipping1 <- read_csv("https://data.london.gov.uk/download/fly-tipping-incidents/536278ff-a391-4f20-bc79-9e705c9b3ec0/fly-tipping-borough.csv",
  col_types = cols(
    code = col_character(), area = col_character(), year = col_character(),
    total_incidents = col_number(), total_action_taken = col_number(),
    warning_letters = col_number(), fixed_penalty_notices = col_number(),
    statutory_notices = col_number(), formal_cautions = col_number(),
    injunctions = col_number(), prosecutions = col_number()))

```

## Check for error

An error message came up with the last code so I checked for problems to see if any rows or columns didn't match.The usual cause is that the column names or number of columns in my cols() don’t match the file

```{r}
problems(flytipping1)

```

## Read it with no column types

The error message persisted so I read it with no column types first

```{r}
flytipping1 <- read_csv("https://data.london.gov.uk/download/fly-tipping-incidents/536278ff-a391-4f20-bc79-9e705c9b3ec0/fly-tipping-borough.csv")
glimpse(flytipping1)

```

## Set the types afterwards using the real column names from glimpse():

```{r}
flytipping1 <- flytipping1 %>%
  mutate(across(c(total_incidents, total_action_taken), parse_number))  # add the other numeric columns you see

```

## Convert the rest of the numeric columns

Finish the job. flytipping1 currently has the first two converted.

```{r}
flytipping1 <- flytipping1 %>%
  mutate(across(c(warning_letters, fixed_penalty_notices, statutory_notices,
                  formal_cautions, injunctions, prosecutions),
                parse_number))

```

## Make data long then wide

```{r}
flytipping_long <- flytipping1 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 4:11, names_to = "tipping_type", values_to = "count")

flytipping_wide <- flytipping_long %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = 1:2, names_from = c(year, tipping_type),
              names_sep = "_", values_from = count)

```
